category_title: High-intensity students who rush through tasks and experience math anxiety
minimal_context: The student is using a computer-generated stopwatch to time parachute drops with a Lego man to calculate average descent times.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Today we are going to calculate the average time it takes for two different kinds of parachutes to reach the ground with the Lego man.

STUDENT: Where’s the stool? Where are the parachutes? What will be attached? A Lego man? Cool!

TUTOR: Here are the materials: tape, yarn, plastic bags, and a hole punch. Let's get started.

STUDENT: (Moving fast through the flurry of materials) How about a hippo? Let’s try a giraffe! Which one will hit the ground faster?

TUTOR: Please just use the computer-generated stopwatch to time the drops so we can record the times.

STUDENT: Let’s just tie them all together and watch them all crash into the ground at once!

options.A: Present a visual scale matching numbers and faces to feeling words to check the student's emotions.
options.B: Provide a structured note-taking paper with specific boxes for the parachute drop topic, background, and vocabulary.
options.C: Provide a verbal prompt directing the student to continue explaining the parachute drop activity.
options.D: Allow the student to continue working with the parachute materials without making any verbal comment.
